extra.reason: Walking skeleton done: Clean Architecture .NET solution + EF Core (Sqlite/Postgres-swappable) seeded from source Excel data, paginated GET /employees; Vite/React frontend (TanStack Router/Query, Zustand, shadcn/ui+Tailwind, generated OpenAPI client) rendering it. Backend integration test + frontend RTL/MSW test green, verified live in a browser end-to-end. Code-reviewed (Standards+Spec axes); fixes applied. Postgres migration compatibility explicitly deferred to excel-management-8ui (notes added there).

Employee CRUD done: POST/PUT/DELETE /employees + GET /employees/{id}, GET /departments (prefactor for 9n4). Validation (Name required, Department must exist, Salary non-negative, Join Date valid) enforced server-side (EmployeeValidator) and mirrored client-side (RHF+Zod), field-level errors surfaced in the UI. Delete requires AlertDialog confirmation. UpdatedAt server-only by construction. 12 backend integration tests + 4 frontend RTL/MSW tests, all green. Code-reviewed (Standards+Spec); fixed 2 duplication smells, added missing Join Date validation+test, and caught/fixed a critical locale bug (DateOnly.Parse used current-culture Buddhist calendar on th-TH, corrupting dates — now InvariantCulture+ParseExact). Verified live end-to-end (create/edit/delete) in a browser.

Department Master Data done: GET/POST/PUT /departments (active-only by default, includeInactive=true for admin), soft-disable only (never hard-deleted), name required+unique validation. Admin screen lists all incl. disabled with inline rename+toggle. Employee dropdown offers active only but still renders/saves an existing reference to a disabled department correctly (fixed a real Base UI Select label-resolution bug found via live testing: form now waits for departments to load before mounting). 18 backend integration tests + 7 frontend RTL/MSW tests, all green. Code-reviewed (Standards+Spec); fixed a state-staleness bug where toggling Active could silently persist an unsaved rename. Filed excel-management-ujs.1 (P4) for a minor check-then-act race on name uniqueness — not blocking. Verified live end-to-end in a browser (disable HR, confirm it drops from create dropdown but Charlie Day's existing HR reference still shows/saves).
Implemented JWT cookie auth + Admin/Viewer RBAC; 32 backend + 9 frontend tests green; live-verified in browser; follow-up ujs.2 filed for refresh-token revocation gap
MCP server implemented via ModelContextProtocol SDK; 7 tools delegating to existing Application-layer repositories; 12 smoke tests + full suite green after merge

Server-side search/filter (name/department/status/salary-range/join-date-range, AND-composed) with URL-reflected filter panel; 47 backend + 10 frontend tests green; live-verified combined filtering in browser; fixed a real per-keystroke loading-flash bug and a history-spam bug found during review

Verified against a live Postgres 17 container (docker run --name excel-management-postgres -e POSTGRES_USER=excelmgmt -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=excelmgmt_dev_only -e POSTGRES_DB=excel_management -p 5432:5432 postgres:17-alpine). Found and fixed two real Postgres-specific issues:
1. The Sqlite-scaffolded InitialCreate/AddUsers migrations create tables that "work" on Postgres (TEXT/INTEGER are valid Postgres type names) but with wrong semantics (no auto-increment, boolean columns stored as INTEGER) - added a new PostgresInitialCreate migration retyping columns to native Postgres types (varchar/boolean/date/timestamptz + identity columns), with explicit USING casts for the four conversions Postgres won't do implicitly (TEXT->timestamptz, TEXT->date, INTEGER->boolean x2).
2. That new migration only applies when Postgres is the active provider (migrationBuilder.ActiveProvider guard) since Sqlite shares the same migration history and already has the right shape - Sqlite doesn't understand the raw ALTER...TYPE...USING SQL. Also had to suppress EF Core's PendingModelChangesWarning in AppDbContext.OnConfiguring since the two providers intentionally end up with different column-type models.
Full CRUD (login, create, read, filter) smoke-tested end to end against a fresh Postgres DB; 47/47 backend tests still green on the default Sqlite path. Container stopped/removed after verification.

Merged CI worktree agent's backend-ci.yml/frontend-ci.yml GitHub Actions workflows + Dockerfiles (API + nginx-served SPA) for both projects. Fixed a real flaky test found by running the new 'npm run test' script against the full suite: EmployeeCrudFlows.test.tsx's disabled-department test used a synchronous getByRole right after opening the Base UI Select popup (async/portal render), passing in isolation but failing under full-suite parallel load; changed to findByRole to match the already-correct sibling assertion.

Added Admin-only Employee Import/Export (Excel + CSV). Export: GET /employees/export?format=excel|csv reuses the existing filter query, new unpaged IEmployeeRepository.GetAllAsync (extracted shared filter-building from GetPagedAsync). Status rendered as Active/In Active text in both formats. Import: POST /employees/import (multipart file), validates every row via ClosedXML parsing + reuses EmployeeValidator for Name/Salary/JoinDate/Department rules (Department matched by name against active departments), collects full row-by-row error report, all-or-nothing via single SaveChangesAsync. 7 new integration tests (valid import, mixed valid/invalid commits nothing + full error report, export excel/csv, export round-trip, viewer 403) - 53/53 backend tests green. Frontend: Export Excel/CSV + Import buttons with row-error table on EmployeeListPage, admin-gated; OpenAPI client regenerated; tsc clean; 10/10 frontend tests green. Tradeoff: import matches department by name (case-insensitive) not ID, for round-trip friendliness with the exported file - documented in code.

Built AuditLog domain entity (EntityName/EntityId/Action enum/ChangedBy/Timestamp/Changes-as-JSON) + IAuditLogRepository/AuditLogRepository + GET /audit-logs (AdminOnly, filters by entityName/from/to). Single shared write path: AppDbContext.SaveChangesAsync/SaveChanges override inspects ChangeTracker for Employee/Department Added/Modified/Deleted -- no changes to EmployeeRepository/DepartmentRepository/endpoints. Real bug found+fixed via live Postgres spot-check: a naive one-pass 'add audit rows before base.SaveChangesAsync' captured EF's temporary placeholder key values for Created rows (Id and any FK to a same-batch-new parent showed garbage negative sentinels, reproduced via seed data). Fixed with a two-phase save under one transaction: Updated/Deleted diffs captured pre-save (original values reset after save), entity save runs first to resolve generated keys, then Created diffs/EntityId are read from the now-resolved entry and the audit rows are saved. Migration: scaffolded against the Postgres provider (not the Sqlite default) because the frozen model snapshot was already Postgres-shaped from a prior migration -- scaffolding under Sqlite reverted all existing Users/Employees/Departments columns to Sqlite types in the same migration (destructive, confirmed by EF's own data-loss warning). Verified end-to-end: 54/54 backend tests green (7 new AuditLogTests: create/update/delete each produce exactly one entry, viewer gets 403, unauthenticated gets 401, entity/date filtering), migration applied cleanly to a real Postgres 17 container (Docker) from a fresh DB, and a manual create/update/delete cycle against it confirmed correct types (character varying, integer identity, timestamptz) and correct audit content. Frontend: admin-gated /audit-log route + AuditLogPage (entity-type + date-range filters), nav link added next to Departments; tsc -b clean, existing suite 10/10 green. Tradeoff: audit list has no pagination (ticket only asked for filtering; matches the Department list's precedent) -- add if log volume grows large enough to matter.

infra/docker-compose.yml (Postgres 17 + api + web, GHCR image tags ghcr.io/gurespex/excel-management-{api,web}:latest) and infra/README.md. Verified end-to-end: built local images under the exact GHCR tags (real images don't exist yet since dev hasn't been pushed to origin to trigger CI), ran docker compose up, confirmed via curl and a fresh-context chrome-devtools browser session (no pre-existing cookies) that login, employee list, and Postgres persistence all work through the containerized stack. Kept the frontend on host port 5173 (matching the backend's currently-hardcoded CORS origin http://localhost:5173) rather than changing application code, per the ticket's 'no application source code' scope. Torn down the verification stack (including volume) and removed the locally-built test images afterward.

Program.cs: wrapped Department create/update endpoint bodies in try/catch(DbUpdateException), converting the DB unique-index violation into the same ValidationProblem the check-then-act NameExistsAsync path already returns, instead of an unhandled 500. Added a deterministic regression test (fake IDepartmentRepository throwing DbUpdateException from CreateAsync) rather than a real concurrent-HTTP-requests test — the latter is unreliable against this test factory's shared in-memory SQLite connection, which throws an unrelated 'nested transactions' error under genuine concurrent SaveChangesAsync calls (a test-harness artifact from the shared :memory: connection, not a production concern, since real deployments use pooled/separate connections per request).

Added server-side RefreshTokens table (id, SHA256 token-hash, user id FK, issued/expires-at, nullable revoked-at) checked on every /auth/refresh call. Login and refresh both insert a row for the freshly-minted refresh JWT; refresh now atomically revokes the presented token's row (rejecting unknown/already-revoked/expired-per-DB tokens with 401) before issuing a new pair -- true rotation, a captured pre-rotation token no longer works. Logout also revokes the current refresh token's row. Root-cause fix along the way: JWTs previously had no jti/nonce, so two tokens minted for the same user within the same second-precision exp window were byte-identical, colliding against the new TokenHash unique index -- added a jti claim to every minted token. Migration scaffolded against a real Postgres 17 (Docker), verified to apply cleanly to a fresh Postgres DB via ef database update, and to Sqlite (the test provider) via the full integration suite. Full backend suite: 64/64 green (62 baseline + 2 new: replay-of-rotated-token rejected, and post-logout reuse rejected). No frontend changes needed.
